items.name: Country (of the home address)

needed_by.purpose: Post documents to the employee

items.name: Canton of residence
items.description: The Swiss canton the employee lives in. Step 2 (Home address), right after the country.

needed_by.purpose: Required field 'Canton' for the registration

items.name: First working day
items.description: The date of the employee's first working day at Muster AG, confirmed by the employee because it often moves. The pension insurance start date is derived from it. Step 3 (Employment start).
items.asked_when: Always

needed_by.purpose: Basis for deriving the insurance start date (HR calls it the 'number one' item)
Confirm the agreed start, which often changes

items.name: Nationality
items.description: The employee's nationality (whether they hold a Swiss passport). Used only to decide whether the employee is subject to source tax. Step 4 (Nationality and permit).
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Switzerland (employees living abroad are subject to source tax whatever their nationality)

needed_by.purpose: Swiss nationals living in Switzerland are not subject to source tax
Know up front who must answer the source tax questions

items.name: Permit type
items.description: The Swiss residence permit the non-Swiss employee holds (e.g. B permit, C permit). A C permit exempts the employee from source tax. Step 4.
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Switzerland and is not Swiss

needed_by.purpose: Non-Swiss employees with a C permit are not subject to source tax

items.notes: No source gives the full list of permit types. See OQ-permit-list.

items.name: Civil status

items.name: Spouse's date of birth

items.required_when_expr: child_age_status == "Minor" and ((child_same_household == "yes" and child_custody == "Shared custody" and child_common_household_other_parent == "no") or (child_same_household == "no" and child_shared_custody == "yes") or (child_same_household == "no" and child_parental_care == "yes"))

items.required_when_expr: subject_to_source_tax == true and address_country == "Liechtenstein" and daily_return_liechtenstein == "no"

rules.name: Employee is subject to source tax
rules.statement: An employee who lives outside Switzerland is subject to source tax regardless of nationality. An employee who lives in Switzerland is subject only if they are not Swiss, do not hold a C permit, and are not married to a Swiss national or C-permit holder who lives in Switzerland. Only employees who are subject answer the source tax questions.
inputs: Spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit
rules.expression: (is_set(address_country) and address_country != "Switzerland") or (address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and permit_type != "C permit" and is_set(civil_status) and not (civil_status == "Married" and (spouse_nationality == "Switzerland" or spouse_permit_type == "C permit") and spouse_residence_country == "Switzerland") and (civil_status != "Married" or is_set(spouse_nationality)))

rules.name: Pension insurance start date
rules.statement: The insurance start date is derived from the first working day, not asked. If the first working day is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day. Otherwise it starts on the 1st of the following month. If the first working day changes, the insurance start date must be derived again and the pension fund's date corrected. The result is always the 1st of a month, as the pension fund requires.

table.then: Insurance starts on the first working day

when: is not the 1st of a month
table.then: Insurance starts on the 1st of the following month (e.g. 15.03 gives 01.04)

rules.name: Civil status answer for the source tax calculator
rules.statement: The source tax calculator's civil status question is answered from the employee's civil status, not asked again: Married maps to 'married or registered partnership' (Verheiratet oder eingetragene Partnerschaft). Single, Divorced and Widowed map to 'single, divorced, separated, widowed' (Ledig, Geschieden, Getrennt, Verwitwet).
rules.expression: if_else(civil_status == "Married", "Married or registered partnership", if_else(is_set(civil_status), "Single, divorced, separated, widowed", null))

rules.name: Residence answers for the source tax calculator
rules.statement: The calculator's 'main residence in Switzerland?' and 'country of residence' questions are answered from the country of the home address, not asked again: Switzerland gives main residence in Switzerland. Germany and Liechtenstein give that country. Any other country gives 'other country' (Anderes Land). Switzerland and other countries give the base tariff without more residence questions.

table.then: Main residence in Switzerland: no. Country of residence: Germany (Germany questions follow)
Main residence in Switzerland: no. Country of residence: Liechtenstein (Liechtenstein questions follow)
Main residence in Switzerland: no. Country of residence: other country (base tariff)

rules.expression: if_else(address_country == "Switzerland", "Switzerland", if_else(address_country == "Germany", "Germany", if_else(address_country == "Liechtenstein", "Liechtenstein", if_else(is_set(address_country), "Other country", null))))

rules.name: Church-tax suffix of the tariff
rules.statement: For earned income, the employee's denomination sets the church-tax suffix of the source tax tariff: Y for Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed, N for none or other (e.g. A0Y vs A0N). Replacement income tariffs (G/Q) have no suffix.

when: Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed

rules.expression: if_else(income_type == "Replacement income", null, if_else(confession == "Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed", "Y", if_else(confession == "None or other", "N", null)))

rules.name: Base tariff letter (source tax)
rules.statement: The calculator's base tariff letter: replacement income gives G. Married with a working spouse gives C, married with a non-working spouse gives B. Not married gives A, or H if at least one child is counted with H (child in household, and sole custody or the employee is the main contributor). For employees in Germany the cross-border tariff replaces A→L, B→M, C→N, H→P, G→Q when it applies. The tariff digit is the number of counted children. HR keeps the calculator as the authority for the final tariff.
rules.expression: if_else(income_type == "Replacement income", "G", if_else(income_type == "Earned income" and civil_status == "Married", if_else(spouse_gainful_employment == "yes", "C", if_else(spouse_gainful_employment == "no", "B", null)), if_else(income_type == "Earned income" and is_set(civil_status), if_else(child_custody == "Sole custody" or (child_same_household == "yes" and child_main_financial_contributor == "The employee"), "H", "A"), null)))

rules.name: Questionnaire flow overview
rules.statement: The questionnaire runs in this order, each step only with the questions that apply: 1 Personal details (first name, last name, date of birth). 2 Home address (street, house number, postcode, town, country, and the canton if the employee lives in Switzerland). 3 Employment start (confirm the first working day, from which the insurance start date is derived). 4 Nationality and permit (only if the employee lives in Switzerland: nationality, and the permit if not Swiss). 5 Family (civil status. Spouse's date of birth if married. Spouse's nationality, permit and residence only if married and otherwise subject to source tax). 6 Source tax (only if subject to source tax: type of income, denomination, spouse works, children and one block per child, then the Germany or Liechtenstein cross-border questions). Address comes before nationality because employees living abroad need no nationality question. Civil status comes before the spouse questions.

open_questions.question: How should an employee in a registered partnership answer civil status, and do the pension fund and the source tax spouse exemption treat them like married employees (partner's date of birth, partner's nationality/permit/residence)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The pension fund list (Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed) has no registered partnership, but the calculator groups it with married, and such employees exist (Daniel). Without an answer they cannot be registered correctly.
options: Ask them to choose 'Married' and treat them as married everywhere
Ask the pension fund how to register them and keep a separate answer for source tax
Ask HR to handle it manually
open_questions.recommendation: Ask Pensionskasse Muster via HR. Until then, treat registered partners as Married for both parties, because the calculator explicitly groups them together.

open_questions.question: Which civil status should a separated (still married) employee choose? The calculator groups 'separated' with single, but the pension fund has no such option.
open_questions.why_it_matters: A separated employee would pick Married for the pension fund and get the married source tax path, which may differ from the calculator's grouping.
options: Married for the pension fund, plus an extra 'separated' question for source tax only
open_questions.recommendation: Confirm with HR. Do not add a question until then.

open_questions.question: Does the pension fund ask for any spouse data when civil status is Divorced or Widowed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: No screenshot shows these cases. Asking too little could block the registration.
options: Spouse's date of birth also appears
open_questions.recommendation: Assume no extra fields. Verify with a screenshot of these two cases.

open_questions.question: Does the pension fund's 'Canton' mean canton of residence or of work, and what is entered for employees who live abroad (Germany, Liechtenstein)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The field is required, but the list only has the 26 Swiss cantons. Cross-border employees could not be registered.
options: Canton of residence; ask the fund what to enter for residents abroad
Canton of work (e.g. Zurich), so it is not asked of the employee
open_questions.recommendation: Ask Pensionskasse Muster. Meanwhile ask the canton only of Swiss residents.

open_questions.question: Which permit types should the employee and spouse be able to choose from, and how does a spouse without any permit answer?
open_questions.why_it_matters: No source lists the permits. Only 'C permit' changes the outcome, but the employee needs a list they recognise.
open_questions.recommendation: Ask HR for the list it uses. The rule only needs to tell C permit apart from other permits.

open_questions.question: Is the consolidated source tax rule complete and does 'here' mean Switzerland? HR hedged ('I think so') before adding further conditions.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The rule decides who sees the whole source tax section and the spouse questions. A wrong rule asks Swiss employees too much or misses people who are subject.
open_questions.recommendation: Have HR confirm the decision table of subject_to_source_tax.

open_questions.question: How should employees with several nationalities, one of them Swiss, answer the nationality question?
open_questions.why_it_matters: HR's rule is 'Swiss passport'. Dual nationals could pick their other nationality and be wrongly sent the source tax questions.
options: Ask 'Do you hold Swiss citizenship?' first
open_questions.recommendation: Confirm with HR that any Swiss citizenship counts as Swiss.

open_questions.question: Is a new employee's income always earned income (Erwerbseinkommen), so the income-type question can be fixed instead of asked?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Asking a new hire about replacement income is confusing and collects unnecessary data. Fixing it also removes the replacement-income cross-border variants.
open_questions.recommendation: Fix to earned income by product decision. Until then it is modelled as asked.

open_questions.question: HR says everyone living abroad is subject to source tax, but the calculator can return 'in principle no source tax liability' for Liechtenstein residents. Which result counts?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It affects what HR does after the questionnaire. It does not change which questions are asked.
open_questions.recommendation: Keep asking these employees all source tax questions and let the calculator result decide. Confirm with HR.

open_questions.question: Can a new employee answer 'certificate of residence provided' and 'proof of more than 60 non-return days provided' before starting? To whom are these documents provided?
open_questions.why_it_matters: These questions ask about documents, possibly the 'German forms' HR mentioned. The employee may not have them yet.
options: Ask as yes/no and let HR collect the documents
Ask whether the employee will provide them
open_questions.recommendation: Ask HR how this works today for Stefan.

open_questions.question: Do the child and cross-border paths behave as modelled for every combination? The calculator was only spot-checked for A/B/H cross-border tariffs, more than 3 children, deleting children and special tariffs (e.g. D).
